prompt: Fly a ZonedDateTime across zones: add a Duration, re-read the same instant in the destination zone, and format it as "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm z" in Locale.US.
explanation: A ZonedDateTime is an instant plus the rules of a zone, so adding a Duration moves the instant and the zone rules decide what the clock then reads -- that is why five hours over the spring-forward night advances the New York clock by only four. withZoneSameInstant keeps the instant and swaps the lens, unlike withZoneSameLocal which keeps the digits and changes the instant. Pinning Locale.US on the formatter keeps the zone abbreviation and any text fields stable no matter what locale the machine running the code happens to use.
hints: departure.plus(flightTime) already gives the right instant -- the only thing left is to look at it from the other zone.
withZoneSameInstant(destination) is the conversion you want; withZoneSameLocal would move the actual moment instead.
Build one DateTimeFormatter with ofPattern("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm z", Locale.US) and reuse it; getOffset().getTotalSeconds() is in seconds, so divide by 60.
